title: GPU fleet drain & maintenance schedule (rotation + driver upgrades)
content: Purpose:\nThis sheet captures the planned maintenance windows and capacity-drain procedure for GPU fleet rotations and NVIDIA driver upgrades. Goal is to coordinate minimal impact to latency SLOs and committed Dedicated capacity while enabling rolling-driver updates and hardware rotations.
content_2:
Scope:
- Applies to prod GPU pools across regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1.
- Includes: driver upgrades (NVIDIA 535 -> 540), firmware patches, and server reboots for GPU hygiene.
- Excludes: emergency power/network maint, which follow SRE incident process.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Target maintenance windows are low-traffic periods per region (local midnight to 03:00).
- Dedicated customers with pinned capacity will be notified 72h in advance and may require dedicated maintenance lanes.
- Autoscaling + burst capacity enabled: expect ability to absorb up to 25% temporary capacity loss without SLA breach if spillover routing allowed.

Pre-maintenance checklist (owner: Aisha / on-call infra lead):
- Verify model variants / smaller models available for fallback (linked: ENGINFRA-4209).
- Confirm rolling capacity policy in router (max_drain_pct, cooldowns set).
- Validate snapshots of KV caches for hot-prefixes.
- Prepare quick rollback image for drivers (540 -> 535).
- Slack channel: #infra-maintenance, pager duty runbook attached.

Drain plan (high level):
1) Target batch size per maintenance slot: 10% of region GPU pool (min 2 gpus, max 8).
2) Mark hosts for drain (set maintenance tag in host inventory).
3) Start draining routing for marked hosts: mark unhealthy for new requests, allow in-flight tokens to finish, optional graceful preempt after 30s.
4) Monitor tail-latency; if p99 > target_threshold for > 5 min, pause additional drains and revert routing.
5) Perform upgrade (drivers, firmware), reboot, run health checks, rejoin pool.
6) Wait 5 minutes steady-state, then resume next host.

Per-step expected capacity impact (example for us-west-2 pool of 200 GPUs):
- Stage 0 (initial marking): 0% immediate loss.
- Stage 1 (draining, no new requests): ~10% capacity loss.
- Stage 2 (reboot/upgrade): ~10% capacity loss + transient CPU/network churn on host.
- Overall active capacity during a 4-slot window: 60-80% depending on concurrency.

Maintenance schedule (recommended rolling windows):
Region | Local Window | UTC Window | Concurrent drain target | Estimated impacted GPUs
us-west-2 | 00:00-03:00 PDT | 07:00-10:00 UTC | 10% per slot | 20 (per 200 pool)
us-east-1 | 01:00-04:00 EDT | 05:00-08:00 UTC | 10% per slot | 18 (per 180 pool)
eu-west-1 | 00:30-03:30 GMT | 00:30-03:30 UTC | 8% per slot | 12 (per 150 pool)
ap-northeast-1 | 23:00-02:00 JST | 14:00-17:00 UTC | 12% per slot | 24 (per 200 pool)

Detailed runbook (commands / checks):
- Mark host for maintenance: curl -X POST https://api.internal/hosts/{host_id}/tags -d '{"tag":"maintenance"}'
- Drain routing: python infra_tools/drain_host.py --host {host} --grace 30 --allow-inflight
- Monitor queues: kubectl -n inference get hpa, svc --watch (or use console per-route dashboard)
- Upgrade driver: ssh root@{host} sudo /opt/nvidia/install-driver 540.sh && sudo reboot
- Post-upgrade health: /opt/infra/check_gpu_health.sh && curl -sS https://api.internal/hosts/{host}/health | jq .status

Monitoring thresholds and rollback triggers:
- If p99 latency increases by >35% for 5 consecutive minutes after a slot start => pause drains and scale up spare capacity.
- If error-rate for generation calls increases > 2x baseline for >3m => roll back driver on last-upgraded host.
- If disk pressure > 85% on any host during maintenance => investigate and hold further upgrades.

Rollback plan:
- Use pre-built driver rollback artifact: s3://infra-artifacts/drivers/540-to-535-rollback.tar.gz
- Steps: pull rollback, install driver 535, reboot, validate model serving smoke tests (end-to-end fast path).
- If rollback fails on >2 hosts in a region, stop the maintenance and open an incident (page SRE lead).

Customer and internal comms templates (short):
- External (Dedicated customers): "Planned maintenance: GPU driver upgrades in us-west-2 on 2026-03-10 00:00-03:00 PDT. We anticipate up to 10% of pinned capacity to be temporarily unavailable; we will not change committed throughput guarantees; please contact success@redwood.ai for concerns."
- Internal Slack: "Starting GPU drain window for us-west-2 in 10m. Draining hosts: host-122, host-145. Monitor #infra-maintenance. On-call: Marco. Escalation: Sanaa."

Post-maintenance validation (owners: Marco + Jingwei):
- Confirm per-route token rates within 95% of pre-maintenance baseline.
- Confirm KV cache hit-rate restored.
- Run 50 synthetic prompts across the GPU variants; compare output latencies and errors.
- Produce short incident-free report within 6 hours: include updated capacity numbers, any driver anomalies, and lessoned learned.

Special notes:
- For Dedicated pools with strict SLAs, schedule maintenance in isolated lanes: spin up temporary short-lived spare machines in alternate region and route traffic with strict geo-policy.
- For on-prem/private deployments, coordinate with customer ops; provide early-access rollback images.
- For major driver bumps (major semver change), run canary on 3 hosts for 24h prior to wide rollout.

Appendix: quick risk matrix
- Risk: p99 spike -> Mitigation: pause drains + autoscale to burst -> Owner: SRE
- Risk: driver incompatibility with kernel -> Mitigation: kernel-driver compatibility pre-checks, rollback artifact -> Owner: platform-eng
- Risk: Dedicated customer throughput hit -> Mitigation: scheduled isolated lane + customer notice -> Owner: customer-success
content_3: Notes: This document is a working planning sheet. Expect iterative updates as canary results and customer feedback come in. Use linked artifacts for automation scripts and test results.
